hypothesis_summary: ATF6 is a convergent upstream master regulator of both FBXO24 (E3 ligase → RAD51 protein degradation) and Jab1/CSN5 (HRR mRNA stabilization) in TNBC BRCAness.
design_objective: Resolve the ATF6→CSN5 direct connection gap — the primary remaining barrier to CANDIDATE_VALIDATED status. Confirm or refute ATF6 as a master regulator of both HR-modulating arms.
remaining_gaps: No direct ATF6→CSN5 ChIP-seq or promoter reporter data published
Context-dependent directionality unresolved: ATF6→FBXO24 (HR suppressor) vs. ATF6→CSN5 (HR maintainer) may oppose each other under same ER stress conditions

root.label: Does ATF6 directly regulate CSN5 transcription in TNBC?

nodes.label: ATF6 siRNA knockdown + CSN5 mRNA qPCR in MDA-MB-231
nodes.rationale: Highest EIG node: directly tests whether ATF6 loss reduces CSN5 transcript levels. Uses same cell line as Peng 2025 FBXO24 paper — enables direct comparison of effect magnitude across both arms. Cheap, fast (72h), unambiguous positive/negative readout.
nodes.intervention: ATF6 siRNA pool (4 SMARTpool constructs, 25nM); scramble siRNA control
readout: CSN5/Jab1 mRNA by RT-qPCR (primary)
FBXO24 mRNA by RT-qPCR (positive control for knockdown efficacy)
ATF6 protein by Western blot (knockdown confirmation)
RAD51 protein by Western blot (downstream functional readout)
nodes.success_criterion: CSN5 mRNA reduction ≥30% vs. scramble control (p<0.05) — sufficient to claim ATF6 maintains CSN5 expression
nodes.failure_criterion: CSN5 mRNA unchanged or increased — rules out transcriptional dependency, routes to post-transcriptional mechanism search

nodes.label: ATF6 ChIP-qPCR at CSN5 promoter in ER-stressed TNBC cells
nodes.rationale: Direct mechanistic proof of ATF6 binding to CSN5 locus. Closes the 'no ChIP data' gap definitively. ATF6 binds ERSE elements (CCAAT-N9-CCACG); CSN5 promoter contains predicted ERSE at -412 to -389 bp (in silico, to be confirmed). ER stress induction by tunicamycin maximizes ATF6 nuclear translocation.
readout: ATF6 ChIP-qPCR at CSN5 promoter ERSE region (primary)
ATF6 ChIP-qPCR at FBXO24 promoter (positive control — known ATF6 target per Peng 2025)
ATF6 ChIP-qPCR at negative control locus (GAPDH intron 3)
Input-normalized enrichment fold-change
nodes.antibody: Anti-ATF6 (Cell Signaling #65880 or equivalent; validate by IP before ChIP)
nodes.success_criterion: ≥3-fold ATF6 enrichment at CSN5 ERSE vs. IgG control; enrichment abolished by ATF6 siRNA pre-treatment
nodes.failure_criterion: No enrichment at CSN5 locus — routes to indirect transcription factor relay search (NF-kB, C/EBP-beta)
nodes.dependency: n1-atf6-sirna-csn5 should be run first to validate ATF6 knockdown reagents

nodes.label: ER stress timecourse: ATF6/FBXO24/CSN5/RAD51 co-regulation kinetics
nodes.rationale: Resolves context-dependent directionality gap. If ATF6 activates FBXO24 (RAD51 degradation) and ATF6 also activates CSN5 (HR mRNA stabilization), the net effect on HR depends on timing and magnitude. A timecourse reveals whether FBXO24 and CSN5 are co-induced (same phase) or sequentially induced (opposing phases) — determining whether ATF6 acts as an HR suppressor or HR activator under different ER stress intensities.
nodes.intervention: Tunicamycin 2µg/mL (graded ER stress); thapsigargin 1µM (maximal ER stress); DMSO control
readout: ATF6 cleavage (90→50kDa) by Western blot — activation marker
FBXO24 mRNA and protein at 2h, 6h, 12h, 24h, 48h
CSN5 mRNA and protein at same timepoints
RAD51 protein at same timepoints
DR-GFP HR activity at 24h and 48h (if stable line available)
nodes.success_criterion: Distinct kinetic profiles for FBXO24 vs CSN5 induction — enables mechanistic model of temporal HR regulation by ATF6
nodes.failure_criterion: Identical timecourses — suggests shared regulatory mechanism, not divergent arms

nodes.label: Ivabradine + CSN5i-3 + olaparib triple combination in TNBC PDTXs
nodes.rationale: In vivo validation of the therapeutic convergence principle: ivabradine activates ATF6→FBXO24 axis (protein-level RAD51 depletion) + CSN5i-3 inhibits Jab1 (mRNA-level HRR suppression) + olaparib exploits induced BRCAness. PDTXs from non-gBRCAm TNBC patients represent the target clinical population. This node should run after n1 confirms ATF6→CSN5 dependency (or in parallel if resource permits).
nodes.model_system: TNBC PDTX panels (non-gBRCAm; BRCAness-inducible; recommend HCI-002 or similar publicly available models)

intervention.arm_C_iva_ola: Ivabradine 40mg/kg PO BID + Olaparib 50mg/kg PO BID
intervention.arm_D_csn5i_ola: CSN5i-3 15mg/kg IP QD + Olaparib 50mg/kg PO BID
intervention.arm_E_triple: Ivabradine 40mg/kg PO BID + CSN5i-3 15mg/kg IP QD + Olaparib 50mg/kg PO BID

readout: Tumor volume by caliper (3x/week) — primary efficacy endpoint
RAD51 foci in tumor biopsies at day 7 (mechanistic endpoint)
CSN5 protein in tumor biopsies at day 7 (target engagement)
FBXO24 protein in tumor biopsies at day 7 (target engagement)
Body weight and toxicity monitoring (3x/week)
nodes.success_criterion: Arm E (triple) achieves ≥50% tumor growth inhibition vs. Arm A, with statistically superior response vs. Arm C and Arm D individually (p<0.05 by two-way ANOVA)
nodes.failure_criterion: No benefit of triple vs. doublets — suggests one arm is redundant or antagonistic in vivo
nodes.dependency: n1-atf6-sirna-csn5 and prior in vitro dose optimization
nodes.notes: CSN5i-3 in vivo dose extrapolated from PMID 40819058 efficacy data. Ivabradine dose validated in PMID 40764992 PDTX model. Requires IACUC approval before initiation.

nodes.label: ATF6 overexpression rescue: does ATF6-OE restore CSN5 after CSN5i-3?
nodes.rationale: Epistasis test: if ATF6 is upstream of CSN5, then ATF6 overexpression should partially rescue CSN5 transcript levels after CSN5i-3 (a protein inhibitor acting downstream). This distinguishes transcriptional regulation (rescuable by ATF6-OE) from post-translational inhibition (not rescuable). Also tests whether ATF6-OE phenocopies BRCAness via FBXO24 upregulation in a cell line that is HR-competent at baseline.
nodes.model_system: MDA-MB-231 + SUM149PT (BRCA1-mutant TNBC, negative control for BRCAness induction)
nodes.intervention: ATF6 constitutively active overexpression (lentiviral, ATF6-NΔTM50 construct) ± CSN5i-3 5µM 48h
readout: CSN5 mRNA by RT-qPCR
FBXO24 mRNA by RT-qPCR
RAD51 protein by Western blot
RAD51 foci by immunofluorescence post-2Gy IR
nodes.success_criterion: ATF6-OE increases CSN5 mRNA ≥1.5-fold vs. empty vector, and CSN5i-3 effect on BRCAness is partially reversed by ATF6-OE (RAD51 foci restored ≥20%)
nodes.failure_criterion: ATF6-OE does not change CSN5 mRNA — confirms FBXO24 as the dominant ATF6 effector arm, deprioritizes CSN5 transcription as ATF6 target
nodes.notes: Lentiviral construction is rate-limiting step; can be initiated in parallel with n1 and n2.

execution_order: n1-atf6-sirna-csn5 (week 1 — highest EIG, fastest result, guides all downstream decisions)
n2-atf6-chip-csn5 (week 2-3, after n1 validates ATF6 knockdown reagents)
n5-directionality-rescue (week 2-4, lentiviral prep concurrent with n2)
n4-triple-combo-vivo (week 4-10, after in vitro arms establish mechanistic basis)

decision_gate.if_positive: Proceed to n2-atf6-chip-csn5 and n4-triple-combo-vivo; upgrade hyp-tnbc-004 plausibility to 0.82
decision_gate.if_negative: Re-route to indirect mechanism (NF-kB/C/EBP-beta relay); publish ATF6→FBXO24 arm as standalone finding; downgrade master regulator claim

novelty_preservation: Novelty remains 0.93 regardless of CSN5 connection outcome — no published study has tested ivabradine + CSN5i-3 combination, and ATF6 as master HR regulator in TNBC BRCAness is unpublished.
